observations.explanation: The paper explicitly describes customizable agents integrating LLMs, humans, and tools, a unified conversation interface, and workflows represented as inter-agent message passing and actions (PDF pp. 2–5).

The paper reports the selected MiniWoB++ comparison on twelve clicking tasks and says MiniWobChat did better on four and tied on three; it also describes the set as selected and reports ten instances per task (PDF pp. 15–16). Calling the result limited and competitive is appropriately qualified.

The paper says the QA results are for the first 500 questions and identifies comparison conditions: FiD and Flan-T5 checkpoints were trained on NQ, unlike the other listed methods (PDF pp. 17–18). The stated limitation on conclusions about general superiority follows from these qualifications.

The paper illustrates applications across several domains and task types (PDF pp. 2, 8–9), while describing prompts and model configurations as adjustable and acknowledging future questions about how multi-agent workflows help and what workflow is optimal for a task (PDF pp. 4, 23). The claim is carefully framed as an unresolved attribution question, not a demonstrated defect.
